name: ai-token-alternatives

frames.best_why: Alternatives panel is open with the ticked word and three options, each with a probability bar.

tagline: Dotted words in an AI reply open a list of the alternatives it weighed.
summary: An AI answer marks words the model was unsure about with a dotted underline. Clicking one opens a small panel of the other words it considered, each with a probability bar; choosing one rewrites the reply from that word on.
appearance: A chat card on dark: a grey user bubble at top right, then the reply in body text where some words carry a dotted underline. The floating panel lists options in a column, each with a thin orange or grey bar and a percentage.
behaviour: The answer streams in word by word with a blinking cursor. Clicking a dotted word opens a panel with the current word ticked; picking another swaps it, re-streams the rest and leaves a small edit chip in the footer. A Confidence switch tints words by uncertainty.
demo_content: A reply about scheduling a launch review for Thursday at 2pm, with swaps for Sure, Thursday, 2pm and 30 minutes.
search_phrases: click a word to swap it
choose between words the ai considered
token likelihood popup under a word
use_when: An AI answer should show where it was uncertain and let the reader swap a word without retyping the prompt.
avoid_when: It is built as a chat card with a prompt bubble and footer, and needs a compose function to regenerate after a pick.
customise: Pass a prompt, slot options with probabilities and a compose function that rebuilds the answer; className is the only style hook. The chat layout and demo copy live in the source.
weight_why: Plain text tokens, one small panel and short springs; the typing timer stops once the answer is out.

a11y.note: Word buttons carry probability labels, the listbox handles arrow keys and Escape, and a live region announces updates.

props.name: compose
props.type: (choice: Record<string, string>, signal: AbortSignal) => ComposedAnswer | Promise<ComposedAnswer>

issues: The alternatives panel covers the sentence it opened from, hiding nearby words until it closes.
polish_why: Coherent detail from dotted words to probability bars; the panel covers part of the reply.
